objects.description: Base exception class for the utf8 library; derives from std::exception. It carries no state and serves as a common base for all library-specific exceptions.
Exception thrown when a Unicode code point is invalid. Stores the offending code point in 32-bit form.
Exception thrown on malformed UTF-8 input. Captures the offending octet.
Exception thrown on malformed UTF-16 input. Captures the offending 16-bit word.
Exception indicating insufficient input/output range or buffer space for an operation (e.g., decoding/encoding needs more octets/words).
Unsigned 8-bit UTF code unit type used by the library for UTF-8 octets. On C++20 and later it aliases char8_t; otherwise it aliases unsigned char.
16-bit UTF code unit type used for UTF-16 words. Aliases char16_t on C++11+; otherwise unsigned short.
32-bit UTF code unit type used for Unicode scalar values/code points. Aliases char32_t on C++11+; otherwise unsigned int.

objects.definition: enum utf_error {UTF8_OK, NOT_ENOUGH_ROOM, INVALID_LEAD, INCOMPLETE_SEQUENCE, OVERLONG_SEQUENCE, INVALID_CODE_POINT};
objects.description: Enumeration of error codes returned by internal UTF-8/UTF-16 decoding and validation helpers.

functions.name: utf8::utf16to8
functions.signature: inline std::string utf8::utf16to8(std::u16string_view s)
functions.description: Converts a UTF-16 string view to a UTF-8 encoded std::string. It forwards to the iterator-based utf16to8(begin,end,out) provided by the underlying library and collects the output into a std::string. Typical use: pass well-formed UTF-16 text; receive a newly-allocated UTF-8 string. Error/exception behavior is determined by the underlying iterator-based function and is not specified here.
requirements: Input s is expected to contain well-formed UTF-16 data (with properly paired surrogates and valid scalar values).
Behavior for ill-formed UTF-16 input is unspecified here and depends on the underlying iterator-based utf16to8 implementation.
This function allocates and returns a new std::string to hold the UTF-8 result.

functions.name: utf8::utf8to16
functions.signature: inline std::u16string utf8::utf8to16(std::string_view s)
functions.description: Converts a UTF-8 string view to a UTF-16 encoded std::u16string. It forwards to utf8to16(begin,end,out) and collects results into a std::u16string.
requirements: Input s is expected to be well-formed UTF-8.
Behavior for ill-formed UTF-8 input is unspecified here and depends on the underlying iterator-based utf8to16 implementation.
This function allocates and returns a new std::u16string to hold the UTF-16 result.

functions.name: utf8::utf32to8
functions.signature: inline std::string utf8::utf32to8(std::u32string_view s)
functions.description: Converts a UTF-32 string view to a UTF-8 encoded std::string. It forwards to utf32to8(begin,end,out) and collects results into a std::string.
requirements: Input s is expected to contain well-formed UTF-32 data (each code point a valid Unicode scalar value).
Behavior for ill-formed UTF-32 input is unspecified here and depends on the underlying iterator-based utf32to8 implementation.
This function allocates and returns a new std::string to hold the UTF-8 result.

functions.name: utf8::utf8to32
functions.signature: inline std::u32string utf8::utf8to32(std::string_view s)
functions.description: Converts a UTF-8 string view to a UTF-32 encoded std::u32string. It forwards to utf8to32(begin,end,out) and collects results into a std::u32string.
requirements: Input s is expected to be well-formed UTF-8.
Behavior for ill-formed UTF-8 input is unspecified here and depends on the underlying iterator-based utf8to32 implementation.
This function allocates and returns a new std::u32string to hold the UTF-32 result.

functions.name: utf8::find_invalid
functions.signature: inline std::size_t utf8::find_invalid(std::string_view s)
functions.description: Scans a UTF-8 string view and returns the byte index of the first invalid UTF-8 sequence, or std::string_view::npos if the entire range is valid. Internally calls find_invalid(begin,end) and translates the returned iterator to an index.
requirements: Input s is interpreted as UTF-8.
Returned value is the zero-based byte offset into s, or std::string_view::npos if no invalid sequence is found.
Exact definition of “invalid” follows the underlying iterator-based find_invalid implementation (unspecified here).

functions.name: utf8::is_valid
functions.signature: inline bool utf8::is_valid(std::string_view s)
functions.description: Returns true if the given UTF-8 string view is well-formed, otherwise false. Wraps the iterator-based is_valid(begin,end).
requirements: Input s is interpreted as UTF-8.
Validity criteria are determined by the underlying iterator-based is_valid implementation (unspecified here).

functions.name: utf8::replace_invalid
functions.signature: inline std::string utf8::replace_invalid(std::string_view s, char32_t replacement)
functions.description: Returns a copy of the input UTF-8 string with any invalid UTF-8 sequences replaced by the specified Unicode code point. Internally forwards to replace_invalid(begin,end,out,replacement) and collects output into a std::string.
requirements: Input s is interpreted as UTF-8.
Parameter replacement should be a valid Unicode scalar value (not a surrogate and within 0x0000..0x10FFFF).
Behavior when replacement is not a valid scalar value is unspecified here and depends on the underlying implementation.

functions.name: utf8::starts_with_bom
functions.signature: inline bool utf8::starts_with_bom(std::string_view s)
functions.description: Returns true if the given UTF-8 string view begins with a UTF-8 Byte Order Mark (BOM), otherwise false. Wraps the iterator-based starts_with_bom(begin,end).
requirements: Input s is interpreted as UTF-8.
Only checks for a leading BOM; does not modify the input.

functions.name: utf8::append16
functions.signature: inline void utf8::append16(utfchar32_t cp, std::u16string& s)
functions.description: Appends the UTF-16 encoding of a single Unicode code point to the given std::u16string. Internally forwards to an iterator-based overload (from checked.h) using std::back_inserter to append code units. Use when you need to encode one code point and extend an existing UTF-16 string. Error handling and validation behavior depend on the checked implementation; typically invalid code points are detected.
requirements: s must be a valid, modifiable std::u16string instance; it will be appended to.
cp should be a valid Unicode scalar value in the range U+0000 to U+10FFFF, excluding surrogate code points U+D800–U+DFFF (inferred from name and typical UTF-16 encoding rules).

Callers should be prepared for the underlying checked implementation to signal errors (e.g., by throwing) if cp is not a valid Unicode scalar value; exact exception type/behavior is unknown without checked.h.

functions.name: utf8::utf16to8
functions.signature: inline std::string utf8::utf16to8(const std::u16string& s)
functions.description: Converts a UTF-16 encoded std::u16string to a UTF-8 encoded std::string. Internally delegates to an iterator-based conversion (from checked.h) and collects the result via a back inserter. Use to obtain a UTF-8 byte string from UTF-16 input.
requirements: s should contain well-formed UTF-16, including correct surrogate pairs where applicable (inferred from function name and typical library behavior).
Callers should be prepared for the underlying checked conversion to signal errors on ill-formed input; exact error/exception details are unknown without checked.h.

functions.name: utf8::utf8to16
functions.signature: inline std::u16string utf8::utf8to16(const std::string& s)
functions.description: Converts a UTF-8 encoded std::string to a UTF-16 encoded std::u16string. Internally uses an iterator-based conversion (from checked.h) and appends the result using a back inserter. Use to obtain a UTF-16 string from UTF-8 input.
requirements: s should contain well-formed UTF-8 (inferred from function name and typical library behavior).
Callers should be prepared for the underlying checked conversion to signal errors on ill-formed input; exact error/exception details are unknown without checked.h.

functions.name: utf8::utf32to8
functions.signature: inline std::string utf8::utf32to8(const std::u32string& s)
functions.description: Converts a UTF-32 encoded std::u32string to a UTF-8 encoded std::string. Internally uses an iterator-based conversion (from checked.h) and collects output with a back inserter. Use to obtain a UTF-8 byte string from UTF-32 input.
requirements: s should contain valid Unicode scalar values only (code points U+0000..U+10FFFF excluding surrogates; inferred from function name and UTF-32 rules).
Callers should be prepared for the underlying checked conversion to signal errors on invalid code points; exact error/exception details are unknown without checked.h.

functions.name: utf8::utf8to32
functions.signature: inline std::u32string utf8::utf8to32(const std::string& s)
functions.description: Converts a UTF-8 encoded std::string to a UTF-32 encoded std::u32string. Internally delegates to an iterator-based conversion (from checked.h) and appends to the result via a back inserter. Use to obtain a UTF-32 string from UTF-8 input.
requirements: s should contain well-formed UTF-8 (inferred from function name and typical library behavior).
Callers should be prepared for the underlying checked conversion to signal errors on ill-formed input; exact error/exception details are unknown without checked.h.

functions.name: utf8::invalid_code_point::what
functions.signature: virtual const char* what() const UTF_CPP_NOEXCEPT UTF_CPP_OVERRIDE
functions.description: Returns a constant C-string describing the error for an invalid UTF code point exception. Use when catching utf8::invalid_code_point to obtain a human-readable message.
requirements: May be called on any instance of utf8::invalid_code_point, including const objects.
Does not throw (noexcept as indicated by UTF_CPP_NOEXCEPT).

functions.name: utf8::invalid_code_point::code_point
functions.signature: utfchar32_t code_point() const
functions.description: Returns the offending 32-bit Unicode code point that caused the exception. Useful for diagnostics after catching utf8::invalid_code_point.
requirements: Object must have been constructed with a code point (always true for thrown instances).
No side effects; may be called multiple times.

functions.name: utf8::invalid_utf8::what
functions.signature: virtual const char* what() const UTF_CPP_NOEXCEPT UTF_CPP_OVERRIDE
functions.description: Returns a constant C-string describing the error for an invalid UTF-8 sequence exception.
requirements: May be called on any instance of utf8::invalid_utf8, including const objects.
Does not throw (noexcept as indicated by UTF_CPP_NOEXCEPT).

functions.name: utf8::invalid_utf8::utf8_octet
functions.signature: utfchar8_t utf8_octet() const
functions.description: Returns the offending UTF-8 octet (byte) associated with the exception. Useful for diagnostics after catching utf8::invalid_utf8.
requirements: Object must have been constructed with a byte value (always true for thrown instances).
No side effects; may be called multiple times.

functions.name: utf8::invalid_utf16::what
functions.signature: virtual const char* what() const UTF_CPP_NOEXCEPT UTF_CPP_OVERRIDE
functions.description: Returns a constant C-string describing the error for an invalid UTF-16 sequence exception.
requirements: May be called on any instance of utf8::invalid_utf16, including const objects.
Does not throw (noexcept as indicated by UTF_CPP_NOEXCEPT).

functions.name: utf8::invalid_utf16::utf16_word
functions.signature: utfchar16_t utf16_word() const
functions.description: Returns the offending UTF-16 code unit (word) associated with the exception. Useful for diagnostics after catching utf8::invalid_utf16.
requirements: Object must have been constructed with a word value (always true for thrown instances).
No side effects; may be called multiple times.

functions.name: utf8::not_enough_room::what
functions.signature: virtual const char* what() const UTF_CPP_NOEXCEPT UTF_CPP_OVERRIDE
functions.description: Returns a constant C-string describing the error for insufficient input/output space during UTF processing.
requirements: May be called on any instance of utf8::not_enough_room, including const objects.
Does not throw (noexcept as indicated by UTF_CPP_NOEXCEPT).

functions.name: utf8::append
functions.signature: template <typename octet_iterator> octet_iterator append(utfchar32_t cp, octet_iterator result)
functions.description: Encodes a Unicode code point as UTF-8 and appends the resulting bytes to the output iterator. Returns the advanced output iterator.
requirements: cp must be a valid Unicode scalar value; otherwise throws utf8::invalid_code_point.
result must be a valid output iterator to a byte container with sufficient space (or capable of growth, e.g., back_insert_iterator).
May write between 1 and 4 octets to result.

functions.name: utf8::append16
functions.signature: template <typename word_iterator> word_iterator append16(utfchar32_t cp, word_iterator result)
functions.description: Encodes a Unicode code point as UTF-16 and appends the resulting code unit(s) to the output iterator. Returns the advanced output iterator.
requirements: cp must be a valid Unicode scalar value; otherwise throws utf8::invalid_code_point.
result must be a valid output iterator to a 16-bit code unit container with sufficient space (or capable of growth).
May write one or two 16-bit code units for BMP vs. supplementary planes.

functions.name: utf8::replace_invalid
functions.signature: template <typename octet_iterator, typename output_iterator> output_iterator replace_invalid(octet_iterator start, octet_iterator end, output_iterator out, utfchar32_t replacement)
functions.description: Scans a byte range presumed to be UTF-8, copying valid sequences to the output and replacing any invalid sequences with the specified replacement code point (encoded as UTF-8). Returns the advanced output iterator.
requirements: start and end must delimit a readable byte range; iteration proceeds forward from start to end.
out must be a valid output iterator to receive UTF-8 bytes.
replacement must be a valid Unicode scalar value; it will be UTF-8 encoded for output.
If an invalid sequence is encountered, exactly one replacement is emitted for that sequence; trailing bytes of the invalid sequence are skipped as per implementation.

functions.name: utf8::next
functions.signature: template <typename octet_iterator> utfchar32_t next(octet_iterator& it, octet_iterator end)
functions.description: Reads the next UTF-8 code point from the byte sequence starting at it, advances it past the sequence, and returns the decoded code point. Throws on invalid input or insufficient room.
requirements: it and end must delimit a readable byte range; it is advanced on success or on certain error paths in internal validation.
On error: throws utf8::not_enough_room if the sequence is truncated at end; throws utf8::invalid_utf8 for malformed sequences; throws utf8::invalid_code_point for illegal Unicode values.
Input bytes from it to the sequence end must be accessible and not past end.

functions.name: utf8::next16
functions.signature: template <typename word_iterator> utfchar32_t next16(word_iterator& it, word_iterator end)
functions.description: Reads the next UTF-16 code point from the code unit sequence starting at it, advances it appropriately, and returns the decoded code point. Throws if there is not enough input.
requirements: it and end must delimit a readable 16-bit code unit range.
Throws utf8::not_enough_room if a surrogate pair is incomplete at end.
May read one or two code units depending on the code point.

functions.name: utf8::peek_next
functions.signature: template <typename octet_iterator> utfchar32_t peek_next(octet_iterator it, octet_iterator end)
functions.description: Returns the next UTF-8 code point without modifying the passed iterator by internally copying it and calling utf8::next.
requirements: it and end must delimit a readable byte range as required by utf8::next.
Subject to the same exceptions as utf8::next for invalid input or insufficient room.

functions.name: utf8::prior
functions.signature: template <typename octet_iterator> utfchar32_t prior(octet_iterator& it, octet_iterator start)
functions.description: Moves the iterator backward to the start of the previous UTF-8 sequence and returns that code point. Throws if at the start or if a valid lead byte cannot be found.
requirements: it must be dereferenceable and not equal to start; otherwise throws utf8::not_enough_room.
start must be the beginning of the valid range containing it.
Underlying iterator must be bidirectional (operator-- used).
Throws utf8::invalid_utf8 if no valid lead byte is found when scanning backward.

functions.name: utf8::advance
functions.signature: template <typename octet_iterator, typename distance_type> void advance(octet_iterator& it, distance_type n, octet_iterator end)
functions.description: Advances the iterator it forward by n UTF-8 code points if n >= 0, or backward by |n| code points if n < 0, using utf8::next and utf8::prior.
requirements: For n >= 0, it and end must delimit a readable byte range; throws per utf8::next on invalid input or insufficient room.

For n < 0, it must be within a valid range whose beginning is end parameter to prior (passed incorrectly as end in code, so callers should pass the true range start when calling prior via this API). Note: In this implementation, backward movement uses utf8::prior(it, end), treating end as the range start. Callers must pass the actual range start as the third argument when using negative n.
Underlying iterator must support decrement if n < 0.

functions.name: utf8::distance
functions.signature: template <typename octet_iterator> typename std::iterator_traits<octet_iterator>::difference_type distance(octet_iterator first, octet_iterator last)
functions.description: Counts and returns the number of UTF-8 code points in the range [first, last) by repeatedly decoding with utf8::next.
requirements: first and last must refer to the same underlying sequence and satisfy first <= last with operator< available (used in loop).
Underlying data in [first, last) must be valid UTF-8; otherwise utf8::next may throw.
Iterator must be at least a random access iterator (operator< used).

functions.name: utf8::utf16to8
functions.signature: template <typename u16bit_iterator, typename octet_iterator> octet_iterator utf16to8(u16bit_iterator start, u16bit_iterator end, octet_iterator result)
functions.description: Converts a UTF-16 code unit range [start, end) to UTF-8, appending to result, and returns the advanced output iterator. Validates surrogate pairs and throws on malformed input.
requirements: start and end must delimit a readable sequence of 16-bit code units.
Throws utf8::invalid_utf16 on lone surrogates or invalid surrogate ordering.
result must be a valid output iterator to receive UTF-8 bytes.

functions.name: utf8::utf8to16
functions.signature: template <typename u16bit_iterator, typename octet_iterator> u16bit_iterator utf8to16(octet_iterator start, octet_iterator end, u16bit_iterator result)
functions.description: Converts a UTF-8 byte range [start, end) to UTF-16, writing one or two code units per code point to result. Returns the advanced UTF-16 output iterator. Throws on invalid UTF-8 input.
requirements: start and end must delimit a readable UTF-8 byte range; the loop uses start < end (random access comparable).
On invalid UTF-8 or illegal code points, underlying utf8::next may throw (invalid_utf8, invalid_code_point, not_enough_room).
result must be a valid output iterator for 16-bit code units.

functions.name: utf8::utf32to8
functions.signature: template <typename octet_iterator, typename u32bit_iterator> octet_iterator utf32to8(u32bit_iterator start, u32bit_iterator end, octet_iterator result)
functions.description: Converts a UTF-32 code point range [start, end) to UTF-8, appending to result, and returns the advanced output iterator. Each input code point is validated by utf8::append.
requirements: start and end must delimit a readable UTF-32 code point range.
Each code point must be a valid Unicode scalar value; otherwise utf8::append throws utf8::invalid_code_point.
result must be a valid output iterator for bytes.

functions.name: utf8::utf8to32
functions.signature: template <typename octet_iterator, typename u32bit_iterator> u32bit_iterator utf8to32(octet_iterator start, octet_iterator end, u32bit_iterator result)
functions.description: Converts a UTF-8 byte range [start, end) to UTF-32, writing decoded code points to result. Returns the advanced output iterator. Throws on invalid UTF-8 input.
requirements: start and end must delimit a readable UTF-8 byte range; the loop uses start < end (random access comparable).
On invalid UTF-8 or illegal code points, utf8::next may throw (invalid_utf8, invalid_code_point, not_enough_room).
result must be a valid output iterator for 32-bit code points.

functions.name: utf8::iterator::base
functions.signature: template <typename octet_iterator> octet_iterator utf8::iterator<octet_iterator>::base() const
functions.description: Returns a copy of the underlying octet iterator position maintained by the utf8::iterator wrapper.
requirements: The utf8::iterator instance must have been constructed with a valid [range_start, range_end] and position within this range (enforced at construction).
No side effects; may be called on const instances.

functions.name: utf8::iterator::operator*
functions.signature: template <typename octet_iterator> utfchar32_t utf8::iterator<octet_iterator>::operator*() const
functions.description: Decodes and returns the UTF-8 code point at the current iterator position without advancing the underlying iterator.
requirements: The current position must be within [range_start, range_end].
Underlying data at the current position must form a valid UTF-8 sequence; otherwise utf8::next invoked internally may throw.
range_end must still be valid for decoding.

functions.name: utf8::iterator::operator==
functions.signature: template <typename octet_iterator> bool utf8::iterator<octet_iterator>::operator==(const iterator& rhs) const
functions.description: Checks equality of two utf8::iterator objects by comparing their underlying octet iterators. Throws if the two iterators were created with different ranges.
requirements: Both iterators must have been constructed with the same range_start and range_end; otherwise throws std::logic_error.
No side effects.

functions.name: utf8::iterator::operator!=
functions.signature: template <typename octet_iterator> bool utf8::iterator<octet_iterator>::operator!=(const iterator& rhs) const
functions.description: Inequality comparison of two utf8::iterator objects; implemented as the negation of operator== and subject to the same range consistency check.
requirements: Both iterators must have been constructed with the same range_start and range_end; otherwise operator== throws std::logic_error.
No side effects.

functions.name: utf8::iterator::operator++
functions.signature: template <typename octet_iterator> iterator& utf8::iterator<octet_iterator>::operator++()
functions.description: Prefix increment: advances to the next UTF-8 code point in the range and returns a reference to this iterator.
requirements: Current position must not be past range_end; decoding the next code point must succeed; otherwise underlying utf8::next may throw.
range_end must remain valid for the lifetime of the iterator.

functions.name: utf8::iterator::operator--
functions.signature: template <typename octet_iterator> iterator& utf8::iterator<octet_iterator>::operator--()
functions.description: Prefix decrement: moves to the previous UTF-8 code point in the range and returns a reference to this iterator.
requirements: Current position must be greater than range_start; otherwise utf8::prior may throw utf8::not_enough_room.
Underlying bytes before the current position must contain a valid preceding UTF-8 sequence; otherwise utf8::invalid_utf8 may be thrown.

functions.name: utf8::unchecked::append
functions.signature:
template <typename octet_iterator>
octet_iterator append(utfchar32_t cp, octet_iterator result)
functions.description: Appends the UTF-8 encoding of the Unicode code point cp to the output sequence beginning at result. Unchecked version: no validation is performed on cp or available output space. Intended for high-performance use when inputs are already known valid.
requirements: cp should be a valid Unicode scalar value (0x0000..0x10FFFF excluding 0xD800..0xDFFF).
result must be a valid output iterator to a buffer with sufficient space for up to 4 octets.
Caller must ensure any required bounds/safety; function does not validate or throw on invalid cp.

functions.name: utf8::unchecked::append16
functions.signature:
template <typename word_iterator>
word_iterator append16(utfchar32_t cp, word_iterator result)
functions.description: Appends the UTF-16 encoding of the Unicode code point cp to the output sequence beginning at result (emits one 16-bit code unit for BMP or a surrogate pair for supplementary planes). Unchecked: no validation or bounds checking.
requirements: cp should be a valid Unicode scalar value (0x0000..0x10FFFF excluding 0xD800..0xDFFF).
result must be a valid output iterator to 16-bit code units with sufficient space for 1 or 2 units.
No validation or error reporting is performed for out-of-range cp.

functions.name: utf8::unchecked::replace_invalid
functions.signature:
template <typename octet_iterator, typename output_iterator>
output_iterator replace_invalid(octet_iterator start, octet_iterator end, output_iterator out, utfchar32_t replacement)
functions.description: Scans the byte range [start, end) assumed to contain UTF-8 and copies it to out, replacing any invalid UTF-8 sequences with the UTF-8 encoding of replacement. Returns the advanced output iterator.
requirements: start and end define a valid input iterator range of octets; iterators must be incrementable until end.
out must be a valid output iterator with enough capacity for the result.
replacement should be a valid Unicode scalar value; it will be encoded as UTF-8 when emitted.

functions.name: utf8::unchecked::next
functions.signature:
template <typename octet_iterator>
utfchar32_t next(octet_iterator& it)
functions.description: Decodes the next UTF-8 code point starting at it and advances it past the decoded sequence. Returns the decoded code point. Unchecked: assumes valid UTF-8 and sufficient remaining bytes.
requirements: it must point to the first byte of a UTF-8 sequence within a valid range; there must be enough bytes until the end for the full sequence (1–4).
Underlying iterator must be incrementable and dereferenceable for each octet in the sequence.
Input must be well-formed UTF-8; invalid sequences result in undefined behavior.

functions.name: utf8::unchecked::peek_next
functions.signature:
template <typename octet_iterator>
utfchar32_t peek_next(octet_iterator it)
functions.description: Returns the code point at it without modifying the original iterator by internally calling next on a copy. Unchecked: assumes a valid UTF-8 sequence at it.
requirements: it must point to the first byte of a valid UTF-8 sequence and be dereferenceable for up to 4 bytes.

functions.name: utf8::unchecked::next16
functions.signature:
template <typename word_iterator>
utfchar32_t next16(word_iterator& it)
functions.description: Decodes the next UTF-16 code point starting at it and advances it past the decoded unit(s). If the current unit is a lead surrogate, consumes the next unit and returns the combined code point. Unchecked: assumes surrogate pairs are well-formed and present when needed.
requirements: it must point to a valid UTF-16 code unit; if it is a lead surrogate, there must be at least one more code unit available and it must be the corresponding trail surrogate.
Underlying iterator must be incrementable and dereferenceable for the needed units (1 or 2).

functions.name: utf8::unchecked::prior
functions.signature:
template <typename octet_iterator>
utfchar32_t prior(octet_iterator& it)
functions.description: Moves it backward to the beginning of the previous UTF-8 sequence and returns that code point. Unchecked: assumes well-formed UTF-8 and that there is a previous sequence in range.
requirements: it must be decrementable at least once and enough times to reach the start byte of the previous code point.
The underlying data before the original it must be valid UTF-8 so that scanning back over trail bytes is correct.
Iterator must be bidirectional (supports --).

functions.name: utf8::unchecked::advance
functions.signature:
template <typename octet_iterator, typename distance_type>
void advance(octet_iterator& it, distance_type n)
functions.description: Advances it by n UTF-8 code points (forward if n >= 0, backward if n < 0) using unchecked next/prior. Unchecked: assumes sufficient range and valid encoding.
requirements: If n > 0, there must be at least n valid code points ahead of it; if n < 0, at least |n| valid code points behind it.
Iterator must be bidirectional when n < 0; forward/incrementable when n >= 0.
Underlying data must be valid UTF-8 across the traversed range.

functions.name: utf8::unchecked::distance
functions.signature:
template <typename octet_iterator>
typename std::iterator_traits<octet_iterator>::difference_type distance(octet_iterator first, octet_iterator last)
functions.description: Counts the number of UTF-8 code points in the half-open range [first, last) by repeatedly decoding next. Unchecked: assumes valid UTF-8 and that first < last advances toward last.
requirements: Underlying iterator must support operator< as used (random-access or pointer-like semantics).
The range [first, last) must be valid and contain well-formed UTF-8 sequences aligned to code point boundaries.
Each increment of first via next must eventually reach last without overrunning.

functions.name: utf8::unchecked::utf16to8
functions.signature:
template <typename u16bit_iterator, typename octet_iterator>
octet_iterator utf16to8(u16bit_iterator start, u16bit_iterator end, octet_iterator result)
functions.description: Converts UTF-16 code units in [start, end) to UTF-8 and appends to result. Lead/trail surrogate pairs are combined into a single code point. Unchecked aside from an early return if a dangling lead surrogate is the final unit.
requirements: start and end define a valid range of UTF-16 code units; any lead surrogate must be followed by a trail surrogate within the range.
result must be a valid output iterator with enough space for the UTF-8 output.
Function returns immediately if the last code unit is an unmatched lead surrogate.

functions.name: utf8::unchecked::utf8to16
functions.signature:
template <typename u16bit_iterator, typename octet_iterator>
u16bit_iterator utf8to16(octet_iterator start, octet_iterator end, u16bit_iterator result)
functions.description: Converts UTF-8 octets in [start, end) to UTF-16 and writes to result. Emits a single 16-bit unit for BMP code points and a surrogate pair for supplementary planes. Unchecked: assumes well-formed UTF-8 input.
requirements: start and end must delimit a sequence of well-formed UTF-8 code points aligned to code point boundaries.
result must be a valid output iterator for 16-bit code units with sufficient capacity.

functions.name: utf8::unchecked::utf32to8
functions.signature:
template <typename octet_iterator, typename u32bit_iterator>
octet_iterator utf32to8(u32bit_iterator start, u32bit_iterator end, octet_iterator result)
functions.description: Converts UTF-32 code points in [start, end) to UTF-8 and appends to result. Unchecked: no validation of code point range.
requirements: Each input value should be a valid Unicode scalar value (0x0000..0x10FFFF excluding 0xD800..0xDFFF).
result must be a valid output iterator with sufficient capacity.

functions.name: utf8::unchecked::utf8to32
functions.signature:
template <typename octet_iterator, typename u32bit_iterator>
u32bit_iterator utf8to32(octet_iterator start, octet_iterator end, u32bit_iterator result)
functions.description: Converts UTF-8 octets in [start, end) to UTF-32 code points and writes them to result. Unchecked: assumes UTF-8 is well-formed.
requirements: start and end must delimit well-formed UTF-8 code points aligned to boundaries.
result must be a valid output iterator for 32-bit code points with sufficient capacity.

functions.name: utf8::unchecked::iterator::base
functions.signature: octet_iterator base() const
functions.description: Returns the underlying octet iterator position wrapped by this UTF-8 code point iterator.

functions.name: utf8::unchecked::iterator::operator*
functions.signature: utfchar32_t operator*() const
functions.description: Dereferences the UTF-8 code point iterator to return the current decoded code point without advancing the iterator.
requirements: The underlying octet iterator must point to the first byte of a valid UTF-8 sequence and be dereferenceable for all bytes in that sequence.

functions.name: utf8::unchecked::iterator::operator==
functions.signature: bool operator==(const iterator& rhs) const
functions.description: Compares two UTF-8 iterators for equality of their underlying octet iterator positions.
requirements: Both iterators being compared should refer to the same underlying sequence type and encoding context.

functions.name: utf8::unchecked::iterator::operator!=
functions.signature: bool operator!=(const iterator& rhs) const
functions.description: Negated equality; returns true if the underlying octet iterator positions differ.
requirements: Both iterators being compared should refer to the same underlying sequence type and encoding context.

functions.name: utf8::unchecked::iterator::operator++
functions.signature: iterator& operator++()
functions.description: Prefix increment; advances to the next UTF-8 code point by advancing the underlying octet iterator by the current sequence length.
requirements: Underlying octet iterator must be incrementable and there must be a complete UTF-8 sequence starting at the current position.
Input must be well-formed UTF-8 across the current code point.

functions.name: utf8::unchecked::iterator::operator++
functions.signature: iterator operator++(int)
functions.description: Postfix increment; returns a copy of the iterator before advancing to the next UTF-8 code point.
requirements: Underlying octet iterator must be incrementable and there must be a complete UTF-8 sequence starting at the current position.
Input must be well-formed UTF-8 across the current code point.

functions.name: utf8::unchecked::iterator::operator--
functions.signature: iterator& operator--()
functions.description: Prefix decrement; moves to the previous UTF-8 code point by stepping the underlying octet iterator backward to the prior leading byte.
requirements: Underlying octet iterator must be bidirectional and decrementable to reach the start of the previous code point.
The data before the current position must be well-formed UTF-8 so that trail bytes are correctly identified.

functions.name: utf8::unchecked::iterator::operator--
functions.signature: iterator operator--(int)
functions.description: Postfix decrement; returns a copy of the iterator before moving to the previous UTF-8 code point.
requirements: Underlying octet iterator must be bidirectional and decrementable to reach the start of the previous code point.
The data before the current position must be well-formed UTF-8 so that trail bytes are correctly identified.

functions.name: utf8::internal::mask8
functions.signature:
template <typename octet_type>
inline utf8::utfchar8_t utf8::internal::mask8(octet_type oc)
functions.description: Returns the low 8 bits of the supplied value, cast to utf8::utfchar8_t. Useful for treating possibly-signed byte types as unsigned when processing UTF-8 octets.
requirements: oc is any integer-like value convertible to an 8-bit quantity.
No side effects; always succeeds.

inline utf8::utfchar16_t utf8::internal::mask16(u16_type oc)

requirements: oc is any integer-like value convertible to a 16-bit quantity.

template <typename octet_type>
inline bool utf8::internal::is_trail(octet_type oc)
functions.description: Checks whether the given octet is a UTF-8 trail (continuation) byte (binary 10xxxxxx).
requirements: oc represents an octet value (0..255). Values outside this range will be masked internally via mask8.

functions.name: utf8::internal::is_lead_surrogate
functions.signature: inline bool utf8::internal::is_lead_surrogate(utf8::utfchar32_t cp)
functions.description: Returns true if cp is a UTF-16 lead (high) surrogate code point (0xD800..0xDBFF).
requirements: cp is a Unicode code point value (0..0x10FFFF).

functions.signature: inline bool utf8::internal::is_trail_surrogate(utf8::utfchar32_t cp)
functions.description: Returns true if cp is a UTF-16 trail (low) surrogate code point (0xDC00..0xDFFF).
requirements: cp is a Unicode code point value (0..0x10FFFF).

functions.name: utf8::internal::is_surrogate
functions.signature: inline bool utf8::internal::is_surrogate(utf8::utfchar32_t cp)
functions.description: Returns true if cp is any UTF-16 surrogate code point (0xD800..0xDFFF).
requirements: cp is a Unicode code point value (0..0x10FFFF).

functions.name: utf8::internal::is_code_point_valid
functions.signature: inline bool utf8::internal::is_code_point_valid(utf8::utfchar32_t cp)
functions.description: Checks whether cp is a valid Unicode scalar value: cp <= 0x10FFFF and not a surrogate code point.
requirements: cp is a Unicode code point value (0..0x10FFFF).

functions.name: utf8::internal::is_in_bmp
functions.signature: inline bool utf8::internal::is_in_bmp(utf8::utfchar32_t cp)
functions.description: Returns true if cp is within the Basic Multilingual Plane (BMP), i.e., cp < 0x10000.
requirements: cp is a Unicode code point value (0..0x10FFFF).

functions.name: utf8::internal::sequence_length
functions.signature:
template <typename octet_iterator>
int utf8::internal::sequence_length(octet_iterator lead_it)
functions.description: Determines the expected UTF-8 sequence length from the lead octet pointed to by lead_it. Returns 1..4 for valid lead octets, or 0 for an invalid lead.
requirements: lead_it dereferences to an octet value (0..255).
lead_it must be dereferenceable; behavior relies only on the lead octet and does not advance the iterator.

functions.name: utf8::internal::is_overlong_sequence
functions.signature: inline bool utf8::internal::is_overlong_sequence(utf8::utfchar32_t cp, int length)
functions.description: Detects whether the given code point cp encoded with a sequence of the given length would be overlong (i.e., not minimally encoded).
requirements: length should be the actual number of UTF-8 code units used to encode cp (1..4).
cp is a Unicode code point value (0..0x10FFFF).

functions.name: utf8::internal::increase_safely
functions.signature:
template <typename octet_iterator>
utf8::internal::utf_error utf8::internal::increase_safely(octet_iterator& it, const octet_iterator end)
functions.description: Advances it by one and verifies the advanced octet is a UTF-8 trail byte. Returns UTF8_OK on success or an error code if at end or if the next byte is not a trail byte.
requirements: it is a valid iterator into the range [begin, end].
If ++it == end, returns NOT_ENOUGH_ROOM and leaves it at end.
If the advanced byte is not a trail byte, returns INCOMPLETE_SEQUENCE.
On success, it points to the validated trail byte.

functions.name: utf8::internal::get_sequence_1
functions.signature:
template <typename octet_iterator>
utf8::internal::utf_error utf8::internal::get_sequence_1(octet_iterator& it, octet_iterator end, utf8::utfchar32_t& code_point)
functions.description: Decodes a 1-byte UTF-8 sequence starting at it into code_point. Does not advance past the lead byte beyond what validate_next() will do later; returns UTF8_OK or NOT_ENOUGH_ROOM.
requirements: it is dereferenceable or equal to end; if it == end, returns NOT_ENOUGH_ROOM.
On success, code_point receives the 7-bit value of the lead octet.
Iterator is advanced within the function as needed for consistency with the family usage; caller should not assume it remains at the original position on success.

functions.name: utf8::internal::get_sequence_2
functions.signature:
template <typename octet_iterator>
utf8::internal::utf_error utf8::internal::get_sequence_2(octet_iterator& it, octet_iterator end, utf8::utfchar32_t& code_point)
functions.description: Decodes a 2-byte UTF-8 sequence starting at it into code_point, validating that the second byte is a trail. Returns UTF8_OK, NOT_ENOUGH_ROOM, or INCOMPLETE_SEQUENCE.
requirements: it is dereferenceable or equal to end; if it == end, returns NOT_ENOUGH_ROOM.
Requires that the next byte after the lead exists and is a trail byte; otherwise returns an error and restores iterator via caller-side logic in validate_next.
On success, code_point contains the decoded value and it is left at the last processed byte prior to validate_next advancing past the sequence.

functions.name: utf8::internal::get_sequence_3
functions.signature:
template <typename octet_iterator>
utf8::internal::utf_error utf8::internal::get_sequence_3(octet_iterator& it, octet_iterator end, utf8::utfchar32_t& code_point)
functions.description: Decodes a 3-byte UTF-8 sequence starting at it into code_point, validating required trail bytes. Returns UTF8_OK, NOT_ENOUGH_ROOM, or INCOMPLETE_SEQUENCE.
requirements: The iterator range [it, end) must contain at least two trail bytes following the lead; otherwise appropriate error is returned.
On success, code_point is set to the decoded value and it points to the last processed trail byte before any outer increment.

functions.name: utf8::internal::get_sequence_4
functions.signature:
template <typename octet_iterator>
utf8::internal::utf_error utf8::internal::get_sequence_4(octet_iterator& it, octet_iterator end, utf8::utfchar32_t& code_point)
functions.description: Decodes a 4-byte UTF-8 sequence starting at it into code_point, validating each required trail byte. Returns UTF8_OK, NOT_ENOUGH_ROOM, or INCOMPLETE_SEQUENCE.
requirements: The iterator range [it, end) must contain three trail bytes after the lead; otherwise returns an error.
On success, code_point is set to the decoded value and it points to the last processed trail byte before any outer increment.

functions.name: utf8::internal::validate_next
functions.signature:
template <typename octet_iterator>
utf8::internal::utf_error utf8::internal::validate_next(octet_iterator& it, octet_iterator end, utf8::utfchar32_t& code_point)
functions.description: Validates and decodes the next UTF-8 sequence starting at it. On success, writes the decoded code point to code_point, advances it to the first octet after the sequence, and returns UTF8_OK. On failure, restores it to its original position and returns an error (e.g., INVALID_LEAD, INCOMPLETE_SEQUENCE, OVERLONG_SEQUENCE, INVALID_CODE_POINT, NOT_ENOUGH_ROOM).
requirements: it is an input iterator over octets in [it, end).
If it == end, returns NOT_ENOUGH_ROOM.
On success, it is advanced past the entire sequence; on failure, it is restored to its original position.
Caller should handle non-UTF8_OK return codes; no exceptions are thrown.

functions.name: utf8::internal::validate_next16
functions.signature:
template <typename word_iterator>
utf8::internal::utf_error utf8::internal::validate_next16(word_iterator& it, word_iterator end, utf8::utfchar32_t& code_point)
functions.description: Validates and decodes the next UTF-16 code point from a sequence of 16-bit words. Accepts BMP code points directly; for lead surrogates, expects a following trail surrogate and combines them. On success, writes the code point, advances it appropriately, and returns UTF8_OK; otherwise restores it and returns an error.
requirements: word_iterator's value_type must be at least 16 bits (enforced via static_assert).
If it == end, returns NOT_ENOUGH_ROOM.
If the first word is a lead surrogate, there must be a following trail surrogate; otherwise returns INCOMPLETE_SEQUENCE or INVALID_LEAD.
On success, advances it past the word(s); on failure, restores it to the original position.

functions.name: utf8::internal::append
functions.signature:
template <typename octet_iterator, typename octet_type>
octet_iterator utf8::internal::append(utf8::utfchar32_t cp, octet_iterator result)
functions.description: Internal implementation that appends the UTF-8 encoding of cp to the output iterator result, using octet_type as the output element type. Produces 1–4 octets without validation of cp.
requirements: result is an output iterator pointing to writable storage for up to 4 octets.
octet_type must be an 8-bit integral type compatible with the container element type.
Caller should ensure cp is a valid Unicode scalar value (<= 0x10FFFF and not a surrogate); otherwise the output may represent invalid UTF-8.
Does not perform bounds checking on the output destination.

functions.name: utf8::internal::append16
functions.signature:
template <typename word_iterator, typename word_type>
word_iterator utf8::internal::append16(utf8::utfchar32_t cp, word_iterator result)
functions.description: Internal implementation that appends the UTF-16 encoding of cp to the output iterator result, using word_type as the element type. Emits one word for BMP code points and a surrogate pair for supplementary planes.
requirements: word_type size must be >= sizeof(utf8::utfchar16_t) (enforced by static_assert).
result is an output iterator with capacity for 1 or 2 words.
Caller should ensure cp is a valid Unicode scalar value (<= 0x10FFFF and not a surrogate).
No bounds checking is performed.

functions.name: utf8::find_invalid
functions.signature:
template <typename octet_iterator>
octet_iterator utf8::find_invalid(octet_iterator start, octet_iterator end)
functions.description: Scans the UTF-8 byte range [start, end) and returns an iterator to the first invalid sequence; if none, returns end. Uses internal::validate_next to advance and check sequences.
requirements: start and end define a valid input iterator range of octets.
Iterators must be incrementable and dereferenceable within the range.
Does not throw; always returns some iterator within [start, end].

functions.name: utf8::is_valid
functions.signature:
template <typename octet_iterator>
inline bool utf8::is_valid(octet_iterator start, octet_iterator end)
functions.description: Returns true if the UTF-8 byte range [start, end) contains no invalid sequences; otherwise false. Implemented via find_invalid.
requirements: start and end form a valid input iterator range of octets.

functions.name: utf8::starts_with_bom
functions.signature:
template <typename octet_iterator>
inline bool utf8::starts_with_bom(octet_iterator it, octet_iterator end)
functions.description: Checks whether the byte range beginning at it starts with the UTF-8 byte order mark (BOM) 0xEF,0xBB,0xBF. Returns true only if all three BOM bytes are present before end.
requirements: it and end form a valid input iterator range of octets.
Requires at least three bytes available to return true; otherwise returns false without advancing the passed iterators (it is a by-value parameter).

generators.generator:
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# This generator produces UTF-8 byte sequences tailored to exercise
# utf8 library functions. It builds well-formed strings spanning 1-4 byte
# sequences, boundary code points, BOM presence/absence, mixed ASCII/non-ASCII,
# and also includes some controlled ill-formed cases (truncated sequences,
# overlongs, lone continuations, isolated surrogates encoded in UTF-8) to drive
# validation and replacement paths. The buffers remain under 4096 bytes.

# Helper: encode a Unicode scalar as UTF-8 (valid scalars only)
def _encode_scalar(cp: int) -> bytes:
    if cp < 0x80:
        return bytes([cp])
    elif cp < 0x800:
        return bytes([
            0xC0 | (cp >> 6),
            0x80 | (cp & 0x3F),
        ])
    elif cp < 0x10000:
        return bytes([
            0xE0 | (cp >> 12),
            0x80 | ((cp >> 6) & 0x3F),
            0x80 | (cp & 0x3F),
        ])
    else:
        return bytes([
            0xF0 | (cp >> 18),
            0x80 | ((cp >> 12) & 0x3F),
            0x80 | ((cp >> 6) & 0x3F),
            0x80 | (cp & 0x3F),
        ])

# Helper: choose a valid Unicode scalar (no surrogates)
def _rand_scalar(rng: random.Random) -> int:
    while True:
        cp = rng.randrange(0x110000)
        if 0xD800 <= cp <= 0xDFFF:
            continue
        return cp

# Predefined interesting valid code points
_VALID_EDGE_CPS = [
    0x0000, 0x0001, 0x0007, 0x0008, 0x0009, 0x000A, 0x001B,
    0x007F,               # boundary ASCII
    0x0080, 0x00A9,       # 2-byte start and symbol
    0x07FF,               # 2-byte max
    0x0800, 0x20AC,       # 3-byte start, Euro sign
    0xD7FF,               # just below surrogate range
    0xE000,               # just above surrogate range
    0xFFFD,               # replacement char
    0xFFFF,               # noncharacter but valid scalar
    0x10000,              # 4-byte start
    0x10FFFF              # max scalar
]

# Some common sequences for variety
_COMMON_STRINGS = [
    "Hello, world!",
    "Café",
    "Привет мир",
    "こんにちは世界",
    "😀😃😄😁😆",
    "a\u0308 o\u0308 u\u0308",   # combining diaeresis sequences
    "ไทย",                         # Thai
    "مرحبا",                       # Arabic
]

# Ill-formed snippets to trigger errors in validators and converters
# Kept short and controlled. These are raw bytes.
_DEFECTS = [
    b"\xC3",             # truncated 2-byte lead
    b"\xE2\x82",         # truncated 3-byte lead (Euro sign lead/trail missing)
    b"\xF0\x9F\x98",     # truncated 4-byte lead (emoji missing last)
    b"\x80",             # lone continuation
    b"\xBF",             # lone continuation
    b"\xC0\xAF",        # overlong for '/'
    b"\xE0\x80\xAF",    # overlong 3-byte
    b"\xF0\x80\x80\xAF",# overlong 4-byte
    b"\xED\xA0\x80",    # U+D800 encoded in UTF-8 (surrogate)
    b"\xED\xBF\xBF",    # U+DFFF encoded in UTF-8 (surrogate)
]

# BOM
_BOM = b"\xEF\xBB\xBF"

def _make_valid_block(rng: random.Random, target_len: int) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    # Start with optional BOM
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        out += _BOM
    # Include some common strings randomly
    for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 3)):
        s = rng.choice(_COMMON_STRINGS)
        out += s.encode('utf-8')
        out += b" "
    # Add a mix of edge code points and random scalars
    edge = _VALID_EDGE_CPS.copy()
    rng.shuffle(edge)
    for cp in edge[:rng.randint(4, min(12, len(edge)))]:
        out += _encode_scalar(cp)
    # Fill up to target_len with random valid scalars
    while len(out) < target_len:
        cp = _rand_scalar(rng)
        out += _encode_scalar(cp)
        if len(out) > target_len:
            break
    return bytes(out)

def _make_invalid_block(rng: random.Random, target_len: int) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    # Optionally prefix with valid text (including BOM) to mix valid/invalid
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        out += _make_valid_block(rng, rng.randint(8, 64))
    # Insert several defect snippets interleaved with valid code points
    defects = _DEFECTS.copy()
    rng.shuffle(defects)
    count = rng.randint(2, min(6, len(defects)))
    for i in range(count):
        # Add a few valid scalars between defects
        for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 3)):
            out += _encode_scalar(_rand_scalar(rng))
        out += defects[i]
    # Optionally end with an incomplete/truncated sequence
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        out += rng.choice([b"\xE2", b"\xF0\x9F", b"\xC2"])  # partial prefix
    # Trim or pad slightly with valid scalars to approach target_len
    if len(out) < target_len:
        for _ in range(16):
            if len(out) >= target_len:
                break
            out += _encode_scalar(_rand_scalar(rng))
    return bytes(out[:target_len])

def _blend_blocks(rng: random.Random, parts: List[bytes]) -> bytes:
    # Interleave parts with small random joiners to create diverse ranges
    out = bytearray()
    for i, p in enumerate(parts):
        out += p
        if i + 1 < len(parts):
            # Add a small random spacer: valid or invalid
            if rng.random() < 0.7:
                out += _encode_scalar(_rand_scalar(rng))
            else:
                out += rng.choice(_DEFECTS)
    return bytes(out)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide overall strategy: valid-heavy, invalid-heavy, BOM-focused, or mixed
    mode = rng.choices(
        population=["valid", "invalid", "bom", "mixed"],
        weights=[3, 3, 1, 3],
        k=1,
    )[0]

    # Choose a target total size, biased small but can be larger up to 2KB
    base_size = rng.choice([32, 64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 1536, 2048])
    target_total = min(4096, base_size + rng.randrange(0, base_size // 2 + 1))

    parts: List[bytes] = []

    if mode == "valid":
        # Strongly valid content with rich coverage
        parts.append(_make_valid_block(rng, target_total // 2))
        # Add many edge points and plane boundaries
        extra = bytearray()
        for cp in _VALID_EDGE_CPS:
            extra += _encode_scalar(cp)
        parts.append(bytes(extra))
        # Add some ASCII runs
        ascii_run = ("A" * rng.randint(1, 50) + "\n" + "Z" * rng.randint(1, 50)).encode()
        parts.append(ascii_run)
    elif mode == "invalid":
        # Heavily invalid with islands of valid sequences
        parts.append(_make_invalid_block(rng, target_total // 2))
        parts.append(_make_invalid_block(rng, target_total // 3))
        parts.append(_make_valid_block(rng, target_total // 6))
    elif mode == "bom":
        # Exercise BOM at start and also mid-buffer positions
        parts.append(_BOM + _make_valid_block(rng, max(16, target_total // 3)))
        parts.append(_BOM + _make_valid_block(rng, max(16, target_total // 4)))
        # Insert a mid-buffer BOM-like sequence surrounded by data
        parts.append(_make_valid_block(rng, 32) + _BOM + _make_valid_block(rng, 32))
    else:  # mixed
        parts.append(_make_valid_block(rng, target_total // 3))
        parts.append(_make_invalid_block(rng, target_total // 3))
        parts.append(_make_valid_block(rng, target_total // 4))

    buf = _blend_blocks(rng, parts)

    # Ensure size limit; also randomly slice a window to vary start positions for iterators
    if len(buf) > target_total:
        buf = buf[:target_total]

    # Occasionally produce a short slice from the middle to vary starting offsets used in stubs
    if len(buf) > 0 and rng.random() < 0.25:
        start = rng.randrange(0, len(buf))
        end = rng.randrange(start, len(buf))
        # Keep at least a few bytes
        if end - start < 3 and end < len(buf):
            end = min(len(buf), start + 3)
        buf = buf[start:end]

    # Ensure non-empty for stubs that assume size>=1 then push a null if empty
    if not buf:
        buf = b"\x00"

    # Final clamp to 4096
    return bytes(buf[:4096])

import random
from typing import List

# We generate byte buffers that the stubs reinterpret as 16-bit code units
# by taking each byte and casting it to utfchar16_t. To exercise UTF-16 logic,
# we build patterns that cover:
# - ASCII and BMP characters (single-word)
# - Proper surrogate pairs forming supplementary code points
# - Lone lead or trail surrogates (to trigger error paths where allowed)
# - Boundary code points and mixed sequences
# - Variable lengths, within a 256-byte cap used by the stubs
#
# The fuzzer stubs:
# - utf16to8(start,end, out): will throw on invalid UTF-16; valid input gives UTF-8
# - next16(it,end): reads one or two words, throws on not_enough_room for dangling lead
# - internal::validate_next16(it,end,cp): success advances it, failure restores it
#
# Our output buffer (bytes) is used by FUZZ_PARAM_STR and then each byte becomes a u16 word.
# So to create specific u16 words, we emit low bytes accordingly; high byte will be 0.
# For surrogate pairs, we must place two bytes that map to the desired 16-bit values modulo 256.
# Because the stubs only take the low 8 bits into the 16-bit word, we construct code units whose
# values are in 0..255. Surrogate range is 0xD800..0xDFFF (>= 0xD800), which cannot be represented
# with only a low byte. To still exercise surrogate handling, we craft pairs where the low byte
# matches lead/trail surrogate low bytes for common values and include a final dangling byte to
# provoke not_enough_room; additionally we include multi-unit sequences with lengths that cause
# validate_next16 to combine or fail depending on implementation that masks 16 bits. Since our
# bytes are promoted directly, we cannot create true surrogate words; therefore, we focus on
# comprehensive valid BMP coverage and truncation cases. We also include zero-length and single
# trailing bytes edge cases via random sizing.
#
# Note: Even though we cannot emit code units >= 256 directly via this stub pathway, the target
# functions still get varied inputs that will traverse different branches for BMP, truncation,
# and iterator behaviors.

ASCII = [
    0x00, 0x01, 0x07, 0x08, 0x09, 0x0A, 0x0D, 0x1F, 0x20, 0x2F, 0x30, 0x39,
    0x41, 0x5A, 0x61, 0x7A, 0x7F
]

# Representative BMP low-bytes (these will be code units 0x00XX in the stubs)
BMP_LO = [
    0x80, 0x85, 0xA0, 0xA9, 0xB7, 0xC0, 0xD7, 0xF7, 0xFF
]

# Bytes that, when used in pairs, simulate multi-unit sequences for next16 length handling.
# We'll just create paired bytes to act as two code units.
PAIR_BYTES = [0x24, 0x26, 0x41, 0x61, 0x80, 0xFF]

REPEAT_SETS: List[List[int]] = [
    ASCII,
    BMP_LO,
    [0x00],
    [0xFF],
    [0x20, 0x20, 0x20],
]

MAX_TOTAL = 256  # stubs cap to 256 bytes for utf16to8; keep overall small


def _emit_ascii(rnd: random.Random) -> bytearray:
    out = bytearray()
    # include a BOM-like UTF-8 prefix in bytes, though they will be individual u16 units
    out += bytes([0xEF, 0xBB, 0xBF])
    # common words
    for b in [ord('A'), ord('z'), ord('\n'), ord(' '), 0x7F]:
        out.append(b)
    # random ascii run
    for _ in range(rnd.randint(5, 20)):
        out.append(rnd.choice(ASCII))
    return out


def _emit_bmp_mix(rnd: random.Random) -> bytearray:
    out = bytearray()
    # mix of control, spaces, punctuation-like low bytes
    for _ in range(rnd.randint(8, 24)):
        out.append(rnd.choice(BMP_LO + ASCII))
    return out


def _emit_two_unit_sequences(rnd: random.Random) -> bytearray:
    out = bytearray()
    # Create many pairs to exercise next16 consuming two units occasionally
    # Although they are not true surrogate pairs, next16 will still advance by one or two
    # depending on implementation; we ensure even and odd lengths.
    n_pairs = rnd.randint(3, 20)
    for _ in range(n_pairs):
        a = rnd.choice(PAIR_BYTES)
        b = rnd.choice(PAIR_BYTES)
        out += bytes([a, b])
    # Append an optional dangling last unit to trigger not_enough_room in some positions
    if rnd.random() < 0.5:
        out.append(rnd.choice(PAIR_BYTES))
    return out


def _emit_pattern_repeats(rnd: random.Random) -> bytearray:
    out = bytearray()
    pat = rnd.choice(REPEAT_SETS)
    reps = rnd.randint(2, 40)
    for _ in range(reps):
        out.extend(pat)
        if len(out) > MAX_TOTAL:
            break
    return out[:MAX_TOTAL]


def _emit_edge_cases(rnd: random.Random) -> bytearray:
    out = bytearray()
    # empty then a null, then a single trailing unit
    out += b""  # no-op, present for clarity
    out.append(0x00)
    out.append(0x41)
    # cluster likely to be interpreted as valid BMP
    out += bytes([0x00, 0x09, 0x0A, 0x0D, 0x20])
    return out


def _shuffle_and_trim(rnd: random.Random, chunks: List[bytearray]) -> bytes:
    # Interleave chunks to create varied sequences; randomize order
    rnd.shuffle(chunks)
    out = bytearray()
    for ch in chunks:
        # sometimes insert a small separator run
        if rnd.random() < 0.3:
            for _ in range(rnd.randint(0, 3)):
                out.append(rnd.randrange(0, 256))
        out += ch
        if len(out) >= MAX_TOTAL:
            break
    # Ensure size within limits used by stubs and overall guidelines
    return bytes(out[: min(MAX_TOTAL, 4096)])


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose a composition strategy
    emitters = [_emit_ascii, _emit_bmp_mix, _emit_two_unit_sequences, _emit_pattern_repeats, _emit_edge_cases]
    n = rnd.randint(2, 4)
    chosen = rnd.sample(emitters, k=n)

    chunks = [fn(rnd) for fn in chosen]

    data = _shuffle_and_trim(rnd, chunks)

    # Ensure non-empty (stubs handle empty, but we want some content)
    if not data:
        data = b"\x00"

    return data

import random
import struct
from typing import List

# This generator produces a UTF-32 code point sequence encoded as raw bytes.
# The fuzzer stub consumes FUZZ_PARAM_STR() to derive UTF-32 code points by:
#   v = (unsigned char)seed[i]
#   cp = (v * 65791 + i) % 0x120000
#   if 0xD800 <= cp <= 0xDFFF: cp = 0xE000
# Therefore, by choosing seed bytes, we indirectly control the distribution of
# code points, including values above 0x10FFFF (up to 0x11FFFF due to modulo),
# which may trigger invalid_code_point exceptions in utf32to8.
# Goal: craft seed bytes that lead to a rich mix of code point sizes and ranges
# (ASCII, 2/3/4-byte UTF-8 ranges within 0..0x10FFFF), edge boundaries, BMP and
# supplementary planes, and some out-of-range > 0x10FFFF to exercise error paths.

# Helper to compute the cp mapping used by the stub for a given byte and index
_DEF_MOD = 0x120000  # as in stub
_MULT = 65791

def _stub_cp(byte_val: int, i: int) -> int:
    cp = (byte_val * _MULT + i) % _DEF_MOD
    # Map surrogate range to 0xE000 per stub logic
    if 0xD800 <= cp <= 0xDFFF:
        cp = 0xE000
    return cp

# We will generate a seed of up to 128 bytes. The fuzzer caps to min(len,128).
# Strategy: build segments targeting desired code point classes after mapping.
# Since the mapping is linear modulo M with relatively large multiplier, we can
# empirically choose byte patterns to statistically cover:
# - Values yielding small cps (ASCII range)
# - Near 0x80, 0x7FF, 0x800, 0xFFFF boundaries
# - Near 0x10000, surrogate edges, 0x10FFFF, and >0x10FFFF
# To keep it deterministic per seed, use Python's random seeded RNG.

BOUNDARIES = [
    0x0000, 0x002F, 0x0030, 0x0041, 0x007F,
    0x0080, 0x00A0, 0x07FF, 0x0800, 0x0FFF,
    0xD7FF, 0xE000, 0xEFFF, 0xFFFF,
    0x10000, 0x10FFF, 0x1FFFF, 0x10FFFF, 0x110000, 0x11FFFF,
]

# Given desired target cp and index, solve for a byte that maps close to it.
# We need x in 0..255 such that (x*_MULT + i) % _DEF_MOD is close to target.
# We cannot invert modulo since x is limited to 0..255, so brute-force the best.
# This is inexpensive (256 tries) and deterministic.

def _best_byte_for_target(target_cp: int, i: int) -> int:
    best_b = 0
    best_err = 1 << 62
    for b in range(256):
        cp = (b * _MULT + i) % _DEF_MOD
        # Apply surrogate mapping to mimic stub effect
        if 0xD800 <= cp <= 0xDFFF:
            cp = 0xE000
        # Prefer exact, otherwise nearest absolute difference
        err = 0 if cp == target_cp else abs(cp - target_cp)
        # If we want to sometimes force > 0x10FFFF to trigger invalid, include those targets too
        if err < best_err:
            best_err = err
            best_b = b
            if err == 0:
                break
    return best_b

# Build a seed byte array assembled from targeted cps and some randomized fill.

def _make_seed_bytes(rng: random.Random, length: int) -> bytes:
    length = max(1, min(128, length))

    # Build a list of target cps we want after mapping. Mix boundaries and randoms.
    targets: List[int] = []

    # Always include BOM boundary related cps and ASCII
    key_targets = [0x0000, 0x0020, 0x0041, 0x007F, 0x0080, 0x07FF, 0x0800, 0xD7FF,
                   0xE000, 0xFFFF, 0x10000, 0x10FFFF, 0x110000, 0x11FFFF]

    # Expand with BOUNDARIES and a few random picks across ranges
    targets.extend(key_targets)
    targets.extend(BOUNDARIES)

    # Add random valid scalar values from various ranges
    def rand_valid():
        while True:
            cp = rng.randrange(0, 0x110000)
            if not (0xD800 <= cp <= 0xDFFF):
                return cp
    for _ in range(20):
        targets.append(rand_valid())

    # Add a few intentionally out-of-range > 0x10FFFF to provoke errors
    for _ in range(10):
        targets.append(0x110000 + rng.randrange(0, 0x10000))  # up to 0x11FFFF

    # Ensure we have at least as many targets as length; if not, pad with random
    while len(targets) < length:
        targets.append(rand_valid())

    # Shuffle targets deterministically
    rng.shuffle(targets)

    # Now choose bytes for each index to approximate target cp after mapping
    seed_bytes = bytearray()
    for i in range(length):
        target = targets[i]
        b = _best_byte_for_target(target, i)
        seed_bytes.append(b)

    return bytes(seed_bytes)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    """
    Generate a bytes buffer intended for FUZZ_PARAM_STR() so that the utf32to8
    fuzzer stub derives a diverse set of UTF-32 code points, including valid
    scalars across ranges and some > 0x10FFFF to trigger invalid_code_point.

    The returned bytes length is up to 128 (fuzzer cap) and <= 4096 as required.
    Deterministic given the provided seed.
    """
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose a length biased towards the cap to maximize coverage, but vary.
    # Use a distribution between 16 and 128.
    length = rng.randrange(16, 129)

    seed_buf = _make_seed_bytes(rng, length)

    # Return directly; the fuzzer will treat this as an opaque string whose
    # individual bytes are transformed into UTF-32 code points by the stub.
    return seed_buf
